findings.finding: Public social records can make stakeholder relationships look more complete or personal than account-level evidence permits.
findings.decision: Keep engagement claims at account level, retain temporal and staff-operation boundaries, and do not publish a relationship graph.

findings.finding: Combining first-person role memory with project-platform custody can overstate individual authorship.
findings.decision: Require explicit first-person attribution or stronger role evidence and preserve collective-work boundaries.

findings.finding: Protected database and attendance aggregates can become identifying or misleading when combined with public social and event traces.
findings.decision: Publish only bounded aggregate units, withhold row-level records and locators, and do not join participant, geolocation, contact, or account data across sources.

findings.finding: The control system could invite identifiable reader feedback into the public repository.
findings.decision: Retain only aggregate findings and coarse action receipts; keep names, employers, applications, and verbatim feedback outside the repo.

findings.finding: Combining protected academic evaluations with public artistic records could expose educational details or convert a teacher's bounded assessment into a lifetime endorsement.
findings.decision: Project only public-safe source summaries, keep grades, identifiers, raw records, correspondence, and recommendation images offline, and state that cross-period continuity is Jamie's interpretation.

findings.finding: Combining a named traveling crew, dated route positions, public invitations, and newspaper photographs can produce a richer movement and relationship record than the portfolio needs.
findings.decision: Name the three-person crew for factual and collective-credit accuracy, retain only coarse route anchors, keep local hosts and passengers unenumerated, and withhold the supplied scan and photographs pending separate rights and participant review.

removalsOrMinimizations: No private path, face tag, GPS payload, participant roster, private correspondence, reader identity, application detail, or raw relationship graph is added by this pass.
The WOW List and Sunday Dinner findings are retained as protected aggregate sources; no user, contact, geolocation, row-level attendance, formula, or account-control record is committed.
The public role policy treats account creation history supported only by Jamie's memory as attributed first-person evidence rather than independent fact.
The technical-operations page omits a duplicate eight-project proof map and limits detailed proof entries.
The About page names public-safe artistic specimens while protected evaluations remain unlinked corroboration with no grade, identifier, contact detail, or raw quotation.
The raft record exposes citation metadata and bounded findings rather than the supplied scan, photographs, local locator, complete route, or a host and passenger graph.
unresolvedRisks: Public reporting and public social records can still reveal affiliations when combined by a determined reader.

This review cannot substitute for collaborator, participant, legal, or human privacy review.
